question: What will the Arctic sea ice extent be on October 17, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Arctic sea ice extent for 2026-10-17 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I couldn't find any forecast or market for October 17 extent. Using the official daily file, extent on September 12, 2026 was **4.574 million km²**, and in 2019-2025 extent grew by 1.12 to 2.07 between September 12 and October 17. The figures below were read from the file through a fetch tool that summarises pages with a smaller model, so a few digits could be wrong. A direct download of the CSV would confirm them.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the daily NSIDC file N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv, which I fetched directly. Its rows run past September 12, but I only used rows up to that date. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- 2026-09-12: 4.574 million km², the lowest value of 2026 so far. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- Recent daily values (million km²), same source:
  - Sept 1: 4.733
  - Sept 3: 4.656
  - Sept 6: 4.632
  - Sept 8: 4.590
  - Sept 9: 4.615
  - Sept 10: 4.609
  - Sept 11: 4.600
  - Sept 12: 4.574
- Earlier 2026 values: 6.495 on Aug 1, 5.354 on Aug 15 and 4.838 on Aug 31. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Extent is flat to slightly falling near the seasonal minimum, and the autumn refreeze has not clearly started.
- In recent years the minimum came between Sept 10 and Sept 18 (shown in heading 4). The value on Oct 17 depends mostly on how fast the refreeze runs from late September into mid-October.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-03: The Met Office reported 7.02 million km² on Aug 2, the 9th lowest for that date. It said ice was exceptionally low in the Kara Sea, well below average in the Laptev and East Siberian Seas, and near average in the Beaufort and Chukchi Seas. July was stormy, and ice was lost at 86,000 km² per day. Note that the Met Office uses a different index (OSI SAF), which usually reads higher than NSIDC. [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- 2026 winter: The winter maximum was a record low, essentially tied with 2025. [ICCI](https://iccinet.org/record-low-2026-arctic-sea-ice-maximum-why-its-essentially-a-tie-with-2025/)

## 4. Base rates
All values are from the NSIDC daily file, in million km².

| Year | Sept 12 | Oct 17 | Change | Daily minimum (date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 4.326 | 5.445 | +1.12 | 4.166 (Sept 18) |
| 2020 | 3.814 | 5.328 | +1.51 | 3.793 (Sept 13) |
| 2021 | 4.776 | 6.842 | +2.07 | 4.757 (Sept 14) |
| 2022 | 4.761 | 6.732 | +1.97 | 4.692 (Sept 15) |
| 2023 | 4.291 | 6.340 | +2.05 | 4.244 (Sept 17) |
| 2024 | 4.247 | 5.713 | +1.47 | 4.245 (Sept 10) |
| 2025 | 4.626 | 6.129 | +1.50 | about 4.54 (Sept 8) |
| **2026** | **4.574** | ? | ? | |

- The change averages about +1.67 (range 1.12 to 2.07, spread about 0.35). Adding each year's change to 4.574 gives 5.69 to 6.64, centred around 6.24.
- 2026 is running just below 2025 and below 2021 and 2022. It is above 2019, 2020, 2023 and 2024.
- Oct 17 values over 2019-2025 ranged from 5.33 to 6.84. Years with slow October refreezes, like 2019 and 2020, were linked to warm water in the Siberian seas.
- Mid-October is when the refreeze is fastest, often 70,000 to 150,000+ km² per day. A refreeze that runs a few days early or late changes the Oct 17 value by roughly 0.2 to 0.5.
- 2025 example of day-to-day noise: 5.961 on Oct 15, 6.060 on Oct 16, 6.129 on Oct 17, 6.213 on Oct 18.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast for Arctic extent on October 17 or in mid-October.
- Polymarket ran contracts on the 2026 summer minimum, with brackets such as 4.4 to 4.6 and 4.6 to 4.8 million km², but none on October values. [Orrery listing](https://orrery.me/markets/will-the-minimum-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer-be-between-4pt4m-4pt6m-square-kilometers)
- 2026-08-03: The Met Office gave a September outlook (on its own index) of about 4.0 to 5.4 million km². [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- The SIPN Sea Ice Outlook covers September only. I did not find its August 2026 median.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The exact minimum date and value are still open. NSIDC usually posts its minimum announcement and refreeze updates in Arctic Sea Ice News in late September and early October.
- Weather matters most:
  - Warm water in the Kara, Laptev and East Siberian Seas, and on the Atlantic side (all low this year), tends to slow the refreeze in those areas.
  - Ice near average in the Beaufort and Chukchi Seas could help extent grow faster on the Pacific side.
- I did not find an official seasonal forecast for Arctic air temperature or refreeze timing covering late September to mid-October 2026.
- The question resolves on the NSIDC preliminary daily value. Data glitches or later revisions to the near-real-time numbers are a small extra source of uncertainty.
